analyst.summary: Astral's FY26 showed a sharp within-year recovery -- from a weak Q1 (PAT -33% YoY, margin 13.58%) to a strong Q4 (revenue +24% YoY, margin ~19.2%, PAT +20% YoY) -- but full-year profit grew only 3% against 13% revenue growth, and the Paints segment ran an operating loss for the year. The bigger overhang is corporate-structure uncertainty: the board approved a chemicals-business demerger into 'Astral Chemie' on 25-Jun-2026 (stock fell 7-11%), then reversed course just 10 days later on 5-Jul-2026, launching its own independent review of the scheme via an external adviser -- a genuine governance-process flag that leaves the plan PENDING, not completed, with no resolution date yet. At 61-70x trailing P/E and 9.3x book against a 14.4% ROE, the market is pricing growth well above what FY26's delivered 3% PAT growth or FY27 management guidance (low-to-mid-teens blended) would support on a reverse DCF -- rich, not cheap. Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter) results are not yet out. Core franchise quality (plumbing leadership, near-debt-free balance sheet, profitable adhesives arm, a helpful PVC anti-dumping tailwind) remains intact, so this is a valuation-and-governance Hold rather than a franchise-quality Sell.
